observationsNotFindings: The corpus-phrase check behaves differently here than in the G26 and G28 joins and is worth recording for whoever reviews the next one. Those harnesses had no namedCorpusNotAuthored field at all, so the subject's local field of that name could not be confused with a source field. G30 v1 does have one, holding three separate members where the subject's identically-named field holds a single phrase. A mechanical field-to-field comparison therefore reports a mismatch on a correct artifact. The subject cites liveHarnessCellVerbatim explicitly as its source, the phrase is an exact suffix of it, and all three harness members appear verbatim inside the phrase - so nothing is lost and nothing is misstated, but the check has to follow the citation rather than the field name.

This is the one join in the family whose recording's cardinality is not stale. D-158 made required-now twenty-six and twenty-six is still live because G30 was the last gate added, so carrying 26 here is correct where the G24, G26 and G28 joins each had to leave their own recording's number behind. The artifact also omits the superseded prior-set figure of twenty-five. Getting both halves right requires knowing which of the two numbers a recording contributes is durable.

Five neighbours are named purely to be disclaimed - DR-101, G14, G16, G24 and G29 - each appearing three times across registerRowNote, authorityClaim and doesNot with no obligation attached. That breadth is proportionate: G30's useful-install selection touches distribution inventory, language runtime, CI, admission and boundary form, so it is adjacent to more live work than any other gate in this sweep, and enumerating the neighbours makes the non-acquisition checkable.

The three EE members this gate owns are closed at D-158 while EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e remain leftover elsewhere, and each of the latter occurs zero times here. DR-117's remainder is therefore larger than this row's obligations suggest, and G30's own remainder is the single fixture-authoring obligation over a three-element corpus phrase.
